# graphic/CLAUDE.md — the graphics engine's rules

Applies to everything under `graphic/`, the crate that draws a graphic clip
(road map 10: `designs/adr/roadmap-10-graphics.md`; the full design is
`archive/roadmap-10.md` §5a). Build commands are the root
`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. It also keeps the face-ID → font-blob map and
  the usage set (`Usage`, `Library::usage()`, spec §11 G-46), filled by
  `select_font`, the wrapped fallback selector and `resolve_string` (image
  kinds only); each closure calls usvg FIRST and only then locks the usage
  set for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same
  thread. The generic families map to bundled faces
  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.
- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and
  the app shows them on the clip.
- `measure.rs` — `FontStyle`, `TextFont` (with `preserve_space`, the
  `xmlSpace` key, G-22), `TextMetrics`, `measure_text`; a generic family
  is written unquoted.
- `module.rs` — `Module` (`Send + Sync + Clone`, holds no QuickJS object):
  `compile`, the SHA-256 revision (G-13), `meta`/`schema` read through
  `JSON.stringify` in the module's key order (`{}` when not exported),
  `defaults()`, its top-level warnings (`warnings()`, G-21 (b)).
- `runtime.rs` — `Engine` (one QuickJS `Runtime` + `Context` per (thread,
  module), §5b's limits, the interrupt deadline), the `thread_local!` map
  swept by `Weak` before each call, at most `ENGINES_PER_THREAD` (16, spec
  §11 G-21) engines with the least recently used evicted after the call,
  `svg`, `Engine::parse_colours` (the stdlib's `__parseColour` per text
  under one deadline, storing nothing; G-25), `engine_count`, `HEAP_BYTES`,
  `STACK_BYTES`, `SVG_BYTES` (8 MiB, spec §11 G-20 (c)). The crate's one
  clock.
- `sandbox.rs` — the sandbox script (G-5) and the loader that resolves no
  specifier, with `IMPORT_REFUSAL`.
- `exception.rs` — QuickJS error → Diagnostic: `{name}: {message}`, the
  position from `stack` (the module's own frame first), the budget's
  sentences, what `render` returned (a string over `SVG_BYTES` refused by its
  length, before the `<svg` check). The texts are load-bearing.
- `host.rs` — the globals `__measureText`, `__assetNames`, `__warn` and
  `__namedColour` (svgtypes' named-colour table for the stdlib's colour
  parser).
- `props.rs` — `check_schema` (compile, strict; it takes a colour reader,
  which `Module::compile` builds from `Engine::parse_colours` over the
  schema's colour defaults, G-25 (a); a non-boolean `animate` on an entry
  is refused, G-41), `overlay` (render,
  lenient; every surprise a warning; an asset stored as `""` is handed to
  `render` as `null`, silently, G-42) and the schema's limits `MAX_PROPS`,
  `MAX_OPTIONS`, `MAX_STRING` and `TYPES`, which the core restates as
  `GRAPHIC_<X>` (`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` pins each pair;
  `tests/reference.rs` pins the numbers the reference states, and its
  typings' key cap).
- `stdlib.js`, `noise.js`, `path.js` — §5c's standard library, evaluated
  as SCRIPTS (globals) in that order before the sandbox; each under 400
  lines. `path.js` is G-31's path helpers (`getLength`,
  `getPointAtLength`, `evolvePath`): pure JavaScript, a curve measured as
  64 chords, a draw-on dashed by the longest subpath, the last paths
  memoised per engine (at most 32, at most 50,000 chords and characters) —
  a cache that changes no answer, held in a closure no module can reach.
  No helper answers `Infinity` or NaN: a path that would make one do so
  is refused in the parse sentence (five checks through one predicate,
  `finite`; `path.test.js`'s row `T8 a number that is not finite`).

## Rules

- **The crate takes bytes and answers bytes** (G-2, G-5): no file system,
  environment or network anywhere in `src/`, and no clock except the call
  deadline. `rg 'std::(fs|env|net)' graphic/src` must print nothing, and
  `rg -n 'std::time' graphic/src` must print exactly one line, the import
  in `src/runtime.rs`: the interrupt deadline stops a call that runs too
  long and feeds no pixel, so a frame stays a function of G-5's inputs.
  Tests may read files and the clock; `src/` may not.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` stays in `lib.rs`.
- Every `src/` file stays under 400 lines.
- Tests are black-box in `tests/`, through `graphic::` only, and every claim
  is an oracle — a pixel read back through `common::pixel`, an exact
  message, a comparison of two answers. The one exception is
  `tests/pins.json` (road map 10 §5l), a tripwire for upgrades.
- The root `CLAUDE.md`'s FFI three-file rule does not apply here: no `rc_*`
  export lives in this crate. G1d's `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs` is its one
  caller.
- **No closure handed to usvg holds the probe lock across a usvg call.** A
  nested SVG asset is parsed by `Tree::from_data_nested` inside
  `resolve_string`, and usvg forwards our `select_font` into that parse on
  the same thread; `std::sync::Mutex` is not re-entrant, so a lock held
  across it hangs the render. Each closure calls usvg first and locks only
  for its own push afterwards. `tests/families.rs`'s nested-asset case is
  the oracle.
- `usvg::Options` is not `Clone`: build it per call with `options()`.
- **`Engine`'s fields drop in declaration order: `render`, then the
  context, then the runtime.** Reversing them aborts the process in
  QuickJS's `JS_FreeRuntime`; `tests/module.rs`'s
  `dropped_modules_engines_are_swept` is the oracle (it SIGABRTs). A
  runtime never leaves the thread that made it, and the thread map's
  `RefCell` is never borrowed while JavaScript runs.
- The module is an ES module evaluated UNWRAPPED, so stack positions are
  the file's own. The standard library and the sandbox are scripts, which
  rquickjs names `eval_script`; `position` prefers the module's frame over
  theirs (`render.rs`'s positioned-throw test and the sandbox's
  `math_random` are the oracles).
- `tests/pins.json` is re-pinned with `GRAPHIC_REPIN=1 cargo test
  --release --test pins`, only after looking at the PNGs a mismatch
  writes to `target/pins/`.
- **The modules of `tests/graphics/` are the bundled templates** (Insert ▸
  Graphic…; project.yml's "Copy Graphic Templates" lists each). Every one,
  the six fixtures included, declares `meta.category` (one of spec §11
  G-45 (c)'s four) and a one-line `meta.description` of at most 120
  characters, held by `tests/template_meta.rs`, where a new template needs a
  row in its `TABLE`. Every one
  except `common::FIXTURES` is held to spec §11 G-44 by
  `tests/templates.rs`: inside title-safe at every frame at 1920×1080,
  1080×1920 and 1080×1080, with defaults, every combination of `enum` options
  and every `string` long (`tests/templates/long_text.rs` must name each), a
  card's background static, the last frame bare, no warning, no `NaN`.
  The six `common::FIXTURES` measure by
  `Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080` (spec §11 VR-43);
  `tests/vertical_templates.rs` holds them inside a 1080×1920 frame inset
  by 24 px, byte-identical to their shipped text at 1920×1080 and
  1080×1080, and holds `app/Sources/GraphicTemplates+Revisions.swift`'s
  table to their current text — an edit of one of the six adds its digest
  there.

## Dependencies, and why each

- `resvg` 0.48.1, `default-features = false`, features `text`,
  `raster-images`, `svgz`: its defaults minus `system-fonts` and
  `memmap-fonts`, which reach the file system — off for G-6 (the fonts are
  the bundled faces and the package's) and G-2 (the crate reads no files),
  NEVER for size. Binary size and build time are not reasons to leave a
  feature out. `raster-images` is required: without it resvg draws no PNG,
  JPEG, GIF or WebP `<image>`.
- `tiny-skia` 0.12.0 (resvg 0.48.1's pin) is VENDORED and patched in
  `graphic/vendor/` (spec §11 PR-13): a dither stage on every gradient, so a
  gradient does not band at 8 bits. Both `graphic/Cargo.toml` AND
  `core/Cargo.toml` carry the `[patch.crates-io]` table — Cargo ignores a
  dependency's `[patch]`, and the staticlib the app links is built from
  `core/` (`a_gradient_is_dithered_through_the_ffi` guards it). The patch is
  `vendor/tiny-skia-dither.diff`, regenerated by the one command in
  `vendor/README.md` and kept byte-equal to the vendored tree; a resvg
  upgrade that moves tiny-skia re-vendors, re-applies that diff and re-pins
  `tests/pins.json`'s gradient entries.
- `serde_json` with `preserve_order`: JSON key order is part of the
  contract (the Diagnostic's and TextMetrics' keys; a module's schema).
- `sha2`: the Library's content version.
- `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg 0.48.1's own pin): parse `font-family` exactly as
  usvg does, so the scan agrees with usvg on what failed; and its
  named-colour table (`__namedColour`), so a colour name means what usvg
  draws.
- `simplecss` 0.2 (usvg's own pin; usvg does not re-export it): read
  `<style>` sheets and `style` attributes as usvg does.
- `rquickjs` 0.14.0 with `loader` only: quickjs-ng 0.16.2, vendored and
  built by `rquickjs-sys`. `loader` exists for `set_loader`; the resolver
  and loader installed refuse every specifier, and none of rquickjs's own
  loaders (which reach the file system) is used.
- `png` 0.18 (tiny-skia 0.12's own decoder, already in the lock): decode as
  `Pixmap::decode_png` does and write the stored copy (G-39); still the
  pins' PNG dump.
- `zune-jpeg` 0.5 (resvg 0.48.1's own JPEG decoder): decode as resvg does,
  so a JPEG's copy is checked against resvg's own pixels.
- `imagesize` 0.15 (usvg's own size reader): check a copy's size reads the
  same as its original's.
- Dev: `flate2`, to gzip an `.svgz` asset in a test.

## Working over MCP

Read `graphic_reference` once. `write_graphic {name, source}` answers `ok` and
`diagnostics`: write again until `ok` is true. `render_graphic {name, frames}`
draws up to 16 frames on a contact sheet with no clip, at most 134217728
pixels of frames in all (two at 8192×8192, or sixteen at 3840×2160);
`add_graphic_clip {name}` places it, `render_frame` shows a frame,
`set_graphic {patch: {props}}` changes it.
`paste_attributes {clips, payload, groups: ["graphic"]}` copies one clip's props onto other clips
drawn by the same module. `import_graphic_font {path}` answers `families`, the exact names
`font-family` must say; `import_graphic_asset {path}` adds a picture for
`asset(name)`; its `name` is the one to use, and `renamed_from` says it was
renamed. `get_graphic` reads a module or names the folder, which your file
tools may edit too; its `API.md` is this page, `API.d.ts` its types.
`get_graphic {}`'s `warnings` says what the folder's scan skipped or could
not watch, such as a file whose name is not a module name. The app keeps the
last 10 texts of each module whenever it sees one replaced: `kept`, in
`write_graphic`'s and `get_graphic {name}`'s answers, lists their revisions,
newest first, and `get_graphic {}`'s `history` lists every name with a kept
text, deleted modules included. `restore_graphic {name, revision?}` writes a
kept text back (the newest by default) and keeps the one it replaced.
`delete_graphic {name}` removes a module no clip draws and keeps its text, so
`restore_graphic` brings it back. `rename_graphic {name, to}` renames a
module and repoints every clip that draws it as one undo step; undo renames
the file back. The folder's `history/` is the app's: leave it to those three
tools. A successful
`export` answers `graphic_warnings`, each distinct warning a graphic gave
while the file was drawn, with its name and frame.

---
title: Graphics with an agent
description: Let an agent write a graphic module, look at its frames, place it on the timeline and check the result, and see what undo covers.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent can make a motion graphic from start to finish: read the API, write the module, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.

Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
  tools={[
    'graphic_reference',
    'write_graphic',
    'render_graphic',
    'get_graphic',
    'list_graphics',
    'insert_graphic',
    'add_graphic_clip',
    'set_graphic',
    'import_graphic_font',
    'import_graphic_asset',
    'add_action',
    'set_action_end',
    'render_frame',
  ]}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab with your Anthropic key."
/>

## The loop

<Steps>

1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` answers it once, for the whole session.

2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` compiles what it wrote and says whether it worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.

3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.

4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The font's answer gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the picture's gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.

</Steps>

## Read the API

`graphic_reference` answers the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.

No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.

## Write a module

`write_graphic` writes `graphics/<name>.js` in the project and answers the compile of that exact text. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and a reader never sees half a file.

A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.

The answer says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still an answer, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as calling `asset()` outside `render`.

Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).

[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.

## A contact sheet

`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.

| Choice | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |

The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.

Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.

A frame that fails is drawn as its error card, and the answer adds a sentence saying where in the module it failed. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.

A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call is refused before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.

:::note
The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
:::

## One frame's SVG

Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` answers one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.

It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is refused. If the frame fails, the answer says so and holds no SVG.

## List and insert

`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.

Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".

`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.

- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The answer names the module the clip is drawn by.
- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call is refused with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.

See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## Place a clip

`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also aim at a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.

| Choice | Default | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |

Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed is refused by its name. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.

Frame Job won't place the clip when:

- The module isn't in the folder. The refusal says what the folder holds.
- The module doesn't compile. The refusal gives its first error.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The refusal names the key.
- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The refusal names the canvas.

## Change a clip

`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).

- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
- **In** can't be set. The trims and splits own it.

These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.

Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.

`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. This is what the **Source** section shows a person.

With no name it reads the folder:

- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.

## File tools

An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |

`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.

In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.

See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.

## Undo rules

The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.

| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |

Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again.

Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts each module replaced, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's text is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

## Graphics in render frame

`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the answer has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## The Assistant

The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).

It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.

## Related

- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)

---
title: Write a graphic module
description: Write your own motion graphic as one JavaScript file, with its name, its properties, the SVG it draws for each frame and the limits it runs under.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic is one JavaScript file whose `render` function returns an SVG picture for each frame. Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
  where={['graphics/API.md and graphics/API.d.ts in your project', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source']}
  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'render_graphic']}
/>

## Try your first module

<Steps>

1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.

3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

</Steps>

A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a legal name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.

## The module

A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
    { clamp: true });
  const y = ctx.height - 200;
  return svg(ctx, `
    <g opacity="${fade}">
      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
    </g>`);
}
```

| Export | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |

`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.

`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.

The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).

## `meta`

Every key is optional.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |

A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.

## `ctx`

`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |

## Resolution-independent drawing

Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.

A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:

```js
const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
```

On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).

## The schema

The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.

| Rule | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |

`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.

## Prop types

| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |

- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
- **`asset`.** `render` gets `null` for both `null` and `""`, so test for it before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.

## Tolerant props

`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.

A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:

```text
props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
```

A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for how those stale rows show in the inspector.

## The SVG the engine draws

Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg. It draws text with the graphics' fonts, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.

An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:

| Warning | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |

description: Write your own motion graphic as one JavaScript file, with its name, its properties, the SVG it draws for each frame and the limits it runs under.

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic is one JavaScript file whose `render` function returns an SVG picture for each frame. Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
  where={['graphics/API.md and graphics/API.d.ts in your project', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source']}
  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'render_graphic']}
/>

## Try your first module

<Steps>

1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.

3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

</Steps>

A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a legal name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.

## The module

A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
    { clamp: true });
  const y = ctx.height - 200;
  return svg(ctx, `
    <g opacity="${fade}">
      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
    </g>`);
}
```

| Export | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |

`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.

`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.

| --- | --- |

| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |

| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |

`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |

Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.

A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:

```js
const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
```

The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.

| Rule | Limit |

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: Graphics with an agent
description: Let an agent write a graphic module, look at its frames, place it on the timeline and check the result, and see what undo covers.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent can make a motion graphic from start to finish: read the API, write the module, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.

Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
  tools={[
    'graphic_reference',
    'write_graphic',
    'render_graphic',
    'get_graphic',
    'list_graphics',
    'insert_graphic',
    'add_graphic_clip',
    'set_graphic',
    'import_graphic_font',
    'import_graphic_asset',
    'add_action',
    'set_action_end',
    'render_frame',
  ]}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab with your Anthropic key."
/>

## The loop

<Steps>

1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` answers it once, for the whole session.

2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` compiles what it wrote and says whether it worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.

3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.

4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The font's answer gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the picture's gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.

</Steps>

## Read the API

`graphic_reference` answers the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.

No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.

## Write a module

`write_graphic` writes `graphics/<name>.js` in the project and answers the compile of that exact text. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and a reader never sees half a file.

A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.

The answer says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still an answer, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as calling `asset()` outside `render`.

Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).

[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.

## A contact sheet

`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.

| Choice | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |

The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.

Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.

A frame that fails is drawn as its error card, and the answer adds a sentence saying where in the module it failed. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.

A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call is refused before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.

:::note
The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
:::

## One frame's SVG

Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` answers one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.

It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is refused. If the frame fails, the answer says so and holds no SVG.

## List and insert

`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.

Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".

`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.

- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The answer names the module the clip is drawn by.
- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call is refused with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.

See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## Place a clip

`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also aim at a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.

| Choice | Default | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |

Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed is refused by its name. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.

Frame Job won't place the clip when:

- The module isn't in the folder. The refusal says what the folder holds.
- The module doesn't compile. The refusal gives its first error.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The refusal names the key.
- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The refusal names the canvas.

## Change a clip

`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).

- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
- **In** can't be set. The trims and splits own it.

These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.

Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.

## Read a module or the folder

`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. This is what the **Source** section shows a person.

With no name it reads the folder:

- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.

## File tools

An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |

`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.

In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.

See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.

## Undo rules

The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.

| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |

Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again.

Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts each module replaced, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's text is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

## Graphics in render frame

`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the answer has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## The Assistant

The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).

It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.

## Related

- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)

---
title: Write a graphic module
description: Write your own motion graphic as one JavaScript file, with its name, its properties, the SVG it draws for each frame and the limits it runs under.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic is one JavaScript file whose `render` function returns an SVG picture for each frame. Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
  where={['graphics/API.md and graphics/API.d.ts in your project', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source']}
  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'render_graphic']}
/>

## Try your first module

<Steps>

1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.

3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

</Steps>

A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a legal name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.

## The module

A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
    { clamp: true });
  const y = ctx.height - 200;
  return svg(ctx, `
    <g opacity="${fade}">
      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
    </g>`);
}
```

| Export | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |

`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.

`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.

The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).

## `meta`

Every key is optional.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |

A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.

## `ctx`

`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |

## Resolution-independent drawing

Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.

A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:

```js
const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
```

On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).

## The schema

The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.

| Rule | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |

`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.

## Prop types

| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |

- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
- **`asset`.** `render` gets `null` for both `null` and `""`, so test for it before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.

## Tolerant props

`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.

A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:

```text
props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
```

A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for how those stale rows show in the inspector.

## The SVG the engine draws

Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg. It draws text with the graphics' fonts, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.

An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:

| Warning | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |

A size mismatch warns too, but the picture still draws: `the SVG is 100×100 but the graphic is 1920×1080`. Using `svg(ctx, body)` for the root element avoids it.

SVG that can't be read at all is an error, and starts `the SVG did not parse:`.

## The sandbox

A graphic can only use its `frame`, `props`, `ctx`, fonts and pictures, so the same frame with the same properties always draws the same pixels. These stop with an error:

| In your module | The error |
| --- | --- |
| `Math.random()` | `Math.random is not available; use random(seed)` |
| `import x from "x"` | `imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global` |
| `new Function("…")` | `Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code` |
| `eval("…")` | `ReferenceError: eval is not defined` |

There's also no `fetch`, no file access, no clock, no `performance`, no `WebAssembly` and no `Intl`. For numbers with thousands separators, use `formatNumber`.

`Date` is frozen. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 1 January 2000 at 00:00 UTC. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).

## Modern JavaScript

Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`, `**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll` and `findLast`.

## The time budget

A runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging Frame Job, because every call has a deadline.

| Where | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Each frame in the preview | 250 ms |
| Each frame in an export | 2 s |
| The module's top level, when it compiles | 250 ms |

Over the budget, the answer is an error such as:

```text
over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError: interrupted)
```

When that error gives a line and column, they're where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.

## Limits

| Limit | Amount | Past it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heap | 64 MB per engine | An error with a line and column |
| Stack | 1 MB per engine | An error with a line and column |
| A graphic's side | 8192 pixels | Frame Job won't draw it |
| The SVG `render` returns | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) | `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most 8388608 bytes` |

`render` must return a string that starts with `<svg`. Anything else is an error:

| What happened | The error |
| --- | --- |
| No `return` | ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?`` |
| A string that isn't SVG | `render returned a string that does not start with <svg at frame 12: …` |
| No `render` exported | ``the module exports no `render` function`` |

A frame that fails draws a red error card on the clip. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for where errors and warnings show.
